content.text: how can i see the date / age of git worktrees

Git does not store a worktree creation timestamp. You can inspect filesystem timestamps:

```bash
git worktree list --porcelain |
awk '/^worktree / {print substr($0, 11)}' |
while IFS= read -r wt; do
  printf '\n%s\n' "$wt"
  stat -c 'created: %w\nmodified: %y' "$wt"
done
```

On Linux, `%w` is the filesystem birth time; it may show `-` if unsupported.

To see the age of the worktree’s current commit instead:

```bash
git -C /path/to/worktree log -1 --format='commit: %ci (%cr)'
```

You can also inspect branch checkout history, if reflogs are available:

```bash
git reflog show --date=iso branch-name
```

These are approximate—Git itself has no authoritative worktree age field.

input.command:
git worktree list --porcelain | sed -n 's/^worktree //p' | while IFS= read -r wt; do
  if [[ ! -e "$wt" ]]; then
    printf '%s\tMISSING\n' "$wt"
    continue
  fi
  created=$(stat -c '%w' -- "$wt")
  if [[ "$created" == "-" ]]; then
    created=$(stat -c '%y' -- "$wt")
  fi
  created_epoch=$(date -d "$created" +%s 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ -n "$created_epoch" ]]; then
    seconds=$(( $(date +%s) - created_epoch ))
    days=$(( seconds / 86400 ))
    hours=$(( (seconds % 86400) / 3600 ))
    age="${days}d ${hours}h"
  else
    age="unknown"
  fi
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$wt" "$created" "$age"
done
